header.running_head: The Hijrah of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jahash (RA)

blocks.text: immediately sold his house in Makkah. Afterwards leather was kept in the house to cure (causing it to stink). When Abu Jahal bin Hishaam, Utba bin Rabee'ah, Shaybah bin Rabee'ah, Abbaas bin Abdil Muttalib and Huwaytib bin Abdil Uzza passed by the house, Utba's eyes flowed with tears as he recited the following couplets (which mean):

"Despite how long it remains intact, every house
shall one day face ruin and desertion"

Abu Jahal then turned to Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) and said, "You people (the family of Rasulullaah ﷺ) have caused these problems for us." When Rasulullaah ﷺ conquered Makkah and entered, Hadhrat Abu Ahmad (Abd bin Jahash) stood up to ask for his house. On the instruction of Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) stood up and took Abu Ahmad aside. (After speaking to him) Hadhrat Abu Ahmad stopped asking for his house.
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was sitting with his body taking support on one hand, Hadhrat Abu Ahmad (RA) recited the following couplets (which mean):

"How beloved a valley is Makkah
where I can walk without a guide
It is there (in Makkah) that my visitors are many
And it is there where my pegs are securely fixed" [^1]

Ibn Is'haaq narrates that after Hadhrat Abu Salama (RA), the first person from the Muhaajireen to arrive in Madinah was Hadhrat Aamir bin Rabee'ah (RA) an Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jahash (RA). Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Jahash (RA) arrived with his family and his brother Abd (who was known as) Abu Ahmad. Hadhrat Abu Ahmad (RA) was blind man who could walk to the upper and lower parts of Makkah without a guide. He was also a poet. His wife was Faari'ah the daughter of Abu Sufyaan bin Harb (RA) and his mother was Umay'ma (RA) the daughter of Abdul Muttalib bin Haashim. The family home of the Jahash family was therefore locked because they had all migrated. Whenever Utba would pass by the house, he would recite some couplets as quoted in the aforementioned Ahadeeth. [^2] It is clear that the Hadith (of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA)) refers to Abd bin Jahash (RA) because it was he who was blind and not his brother Abdullaah bin Jahash (RA). Referring to the Hijrah of his family, Hadhrat Abu Ahmad bin Jahash (RA) recited the following couplets (which mean):

"When (my wife) Ummu Ahmad saw me leaving
in the protection of the One I fear without having seen Him
She said, 'If you have to migrate somewhere
then take us somewhere else far from Yathrib'
I said to her, 'Yathrib is no bad place
and a servant must do what Ar Rahmaan wants'
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.6 Pg.64) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.3 Pg.170).
